summary.headline: Scope your AI to password resets and teammate invites only — ~38% of common intents have no KB article, and three sensitive intents must be hard-gated.
summary.narrative: We mined eight recurring intents from 26 cases. Two (password reset, invite teammates) are cleanly covered and safe to scope in today. About 38% of common intents — API rate limits, API key rotation, webhook troubleshooting — have no KB article at all, so an AI would have to invent answers. Billing disputes, account security, and legal/regulated (GDPR) intents appear repeatedly and must go on an out-of-scope safety list before any AI step.

stats.label: Common intents with no KB article

findings.title: High-volume developer intents have zero KB coverage
findings.what_we_found: API rate limits (CS-1007), API key rotation (CS-1020), and webhook troubleshooting (CS-1008) recur across cases, but no KB article exists for any of them — case notes confirm ‘no KB article exists on limits’ and ‘no article; awaiting eng’.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: With no grounding source, an AI agent would fabricate limits, rotation steps, or fixes — exactly the developer-facing answers that must be precise.
the_fix: Author single-topic articles: API Rate Limits, API Key Rotation, Webhook Troubleshooting.
Keep these intents out of AI scope until the articles are published and reviewed by engineering.
Re-run this mapper after publishing to confirm coverage.
findings.evidence: ~38% of mined common intents have no matching KB article.

findings.title: SSO and Salesforce-connect intents have only stale coverage
findings.what_we_found: SSO setup (CS-1012, CS-1016) maps only to the 2023 SSO Setup article (which also has a dangling reference); connect-Salesforce (CS-1025) maps only to the 2023 integration guide citing an outdated package version.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: The only matching articles are stale, so the AI would ground on facts that are no longer true. Technically covered, not safely groundable.
the_fix: Refresh both articles (hand to KB Retrieval Readiness) before scoping these intents in.
Do not place SSO or Salesforce-connect in AI scope until coverage is current.
findings.evidence: Both matching articles last_updated 2023; one asserts package v1.2.

findings.title: Sensitive intents are recurring and currently unguarded
findings.what_we_found: Billing disputes (CS-1003, CS-1006, CS-1019, CS-1024), account-security questions (security questionnaire CS-1021), and legal/regulated GDPR / data-residency requests (CS-1011) appear repeatedly and are handled ad hoc with no KB and no AI guardrail.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: If an AI self-serves these, it risks giving financial, security, or legal answers it must never give. They require a hard human gate, not model judgement.
the_fix: Add all three classes to the out-of-scope safety list (see draft).
Route each to a named human queue: billing disputes → Billing, security → Security/IT, GDPR/legal → Legal.
Have the CS lead and Legal ratify the list before any AI step.
findings.evidence: 4 billing-dispute cases, 1 security-questionnaire case, 1 GDPR case in the export.

drafts.title: Draft AI out-of-scope safety list (for human ratification)
drafts.content:
Intents the AI must NOT self-serve — acknowledge and route to a human:

| Intent | Why out of scope | Route to |
|---|---|---|
| Billing disputes / refunds / overage / cancellation charges | Financial decisions and contract terms; risk of incorrect refund or commitment | Billing team |
| Account security (security questionnaires, suspected compromise, access changes) | Security-sensitive; must verify identity and follow policy | Security / IT |
| Legal / regulated (GDPR, data residency, tax exemption, contract disputes) | Regulated answers; guidance not legal advice | Legal |

For each, the AI should acknowledge, set expectations, and hand off — never attempt a resolving answer.
grounded_on: fixtures/customer-success/cases.csv (categories: Billing dispute, Compliance, Account access)
